title: Quickstart: fitting an adaptive FFT
text: fit$winner whichever family won inner race; fit$chain shows predicate sequence winning tree.
code: fit <- adaptive_fft(tr, te, dataset_name = "heartdisease",                     baselines = list(`ifan (paper)` = 0.787)) print(fit) #> Adaptive FFT — heartdisease #>   n_train = 211, n_test = 92, base rate = 0.46 #>   Inner race: ifan=0.685  beam-doe09=0.729  → winner: beam-doe09 #>   Chain (depth 2): ca → oldpeak #>   Test: bacc=0.657  acc=0.652  f1=0.652  frugality=1.61 cues #>   Deltas vs baselines: #>     vs ifan (paper)       -0.130

title: Adaptive Fast-and-Frugal Trees with Inner-Holdout Family Selection
text: Adaptive Fast--Frugal Trees — chain decision trees depth ≤ 4 one cue per node binary exits, fit either FFTrees’ greedy ifan algorithm beam search chain space (hyperparameters selected via D-optimal Design Experiments). adaptive_fft() constructor performs inner-holdout race two families refits winner full training set. Companion code Jakel (2026), Adaptive Fast--Frugal Trees: Model-Family Selection Narrows Gap Optimal Sparse Trees Imbalanced Benchmarks (arXiv preprint). Travis Jakel — Asset Flow Capital.

title: Adaptive Fast-and-Frugal Trees with Inner-Holdout Family Selection

title: Fit an adaptive chain Fast-and-Frugal Tree — adaptive_fft
text: train, test `data.table`s binary outcome column `y` (0/1 integers). max_levels Maximum chain depth (1-4). Default 4. inner_frac Fraction training rows allocated inner train half family race. Default 0.80. beam_B, beam_max_thr, beam_item_cap Hyperparameters passed [run_beam_fft()]. Defaults match D-optimal-DoE selected "beam-doe09" configuration: `beam_B = 10`, `beam_max_thr = 5`, `beam_item_cap = 50`. baselines Optional named numeric list baseline test-bacc values Δ panel [plot.adaptive_fft()], e.g. `list(ifan = 0.79, streed4_bacc = 0.81)`. `NULL` omits panel. dataset_name Short label used plot headers.

title: Fit an adaptive chain Fast-and-Frugal Tree — adaptive_fft
text: Object class `adaptive_fft`. List elements:   `dataset_name`, `n_train`, `n_test`, `base_rate`, `winner`,   `scores` (data.table inner-valid bacc per family),   `chain` (data.table winning tree's nodes),   `test_pred`, `test_y`, `test_exits`, `test_bacc`, `test_acc`,   `test_f1`, `test_frug`, `baselines`, `max_levels`, `inner_frac`.

title: Fit an adaptive chain Fast-and-Frugal Tree — adaptive_fft
text: Reproduces procedure described Jakel (2026, §3.2 "adaptive"): adaptive yields +1.4 pp balanced-accuracy point estimate `ifan` across 14 datasets x 20 stratified seeds (rank-biserial r = 0.44), preserving strict chain-FFT structure (depth ≤ `max_levels`, one cue per node, binary exits every level).

text: train, test `data.table`s binary criterion column `y`. max_levels Maximum chain depth (1-4). beam_B Beam width — number partial chains carried forward depth levels. max_thresholds_per_cue numeric cue, top `K` midpoint thresholds marginal normalized MI kept. item_cap Maximum number (cue, direction, threshold) items retained search; pre-ranked marginal balanced accuracy. `Inf` keeps .

text: Initial public release accompanying arXiv preprint “Adaptive Fast--Frugal Trees: Model-Family Selection Narrows Gap Optimal Sparse Trees Imbalanced Benchmarks.” Public API: adaptive_fft() constructor print(), summary(), plot() S3 methods; run_beam_fft() standalone beam search; score_all() metric helper; bundled benchmark results. 14 dataset loaders mirroring FFTrees benchmark suite.
